Changelog

Release notes

Version history for the SignalForge CLI and REST API. Subscribe to releases on GitHub.

v0.9.2
2024-03-10
patch
Webhook retry logic + signal deduplication fix
NEW Webhook exponential backoff. Failed webhook deliveries are now retried with exponential backoff: 1s, 5s, 30s, 5m, 30m. Max 5 attempts per delivery. Delivery status is visible in your webhook log at GET /v1/webhooks/{id}/deliveries.
FIX Signal deduplication edge case. A race condition in the dedup layer could cause a second signal.fired event to be dispatched when monitors recovered and immediately re-failed within a single check window. This is now handled correctly.
IMP CLI status command latency. Reduced signalforge status response time by ~60% by moving monitor state reads to a read replica. Status checks now consistently complete in under 200ms.
FIX YAML interpolation for nested env vars. Environment variable references inside nested YAML keys (e.g., destinations.url) were not being interpolated in v0.9.1. Fixed.
Upgrade bash 
$ npm update -g @signalforge/cli
# or
$ brew upgrade signalforge
v0.9.1
2024-02-22
patch
SSL monitor improvements + CLI UX polish
NEW SSL certificate chain validation. SSL monitors now verify the full certificate chain, not just the leaf certificate. Invalid intermediate CA configurations are now surfaced as a cert_chain_invalid signal.
IMP signalforge monitor sync --dry-run. New flag shows a diff of proposed changes without applying them. Useful for CI validation.
IMP Better signalforge init output. Clearer prompts, workspace name validation, and a generated starter signalforge.yml that includes comments and examples.
FIX TCP monitor false positives in eu-west-1. A DNS caching issue caused TCP monitors to occasionally resolve to stale IPs from our EU probe network. Resolved by pinning probe TTL to 30s.
v0.9.0
2024-01-30
release
Alert Rules Engine — composable multi-signal rules

The biggest feature release since launch. The Alert Rules Engine lets you compose rules from multiple signal types using AND/OR logic, enabling powerful incident correlation patterns.

NEW Alert Rules Engine. Define rules in signalforge.yml under the rules: key. Rules support any_critical, all_critical, any_warning combinators across multiple monitors. Multi-service outage detection is now a first-class primitive.
NEW Maintenance windows. Schedule maintenance windows via CLI or API. Signals during a maintenance window are recorded but not dispatched. Windows support one-off and recurring (cron) schedules.
NEW Signal acknowledgment API. POST /v1/signals/{id}/acknowledge lets you programmatically acknowledge signals and suppress repeat notifications. The CLI command is signalforge ack <signal_id>.
NEW Post-mortem generator. signalforge postmortem --signal <id> --format markdown generates a structured post-mortem template pre-populated with the signal timeline.
IMP Multi-region probes. All monitor types now support up to 4 concurrent probe regions (previously HTTP-only). Configure via the regions array in your monitor definition.
DEP notify top-level key deprecated. The v0.8.x notify: top-level key in signalforge.yml is deprecated in favor of per-monitor alert: blocks and top-level rules:. It will be removed in v1.0.0. Run signalforge migrate to auto-upgrade your config.
v0.8.5
2023-12-14
patch
DNS monitor type + latency percentile improvements
NEW DNS monitor type. Monitor DNS resolution for any hostname. Validates record type (A, AAAA, CNAME, MX, TXT), expected value, and alerts on resolution failure or value mismatch.
IMP Latency percentile tracking. HTTP monitors now track and expose p50, p75, p95, and p99 latency. All four percentiles are available in the signal payload and API response. Previously only p95 was tracked.
FIX Body content check with JSON responses. The body_contains assertion was incorrectly failing on responses with compressed JSON bodies (e.g. when the server returns Content-Encoding: gzip). Fixed.
v0.8.0
2023-11-01
release
Public launch — HTTP + TCP monitoring, webhook delivery

Initial public release of SignalForge. This release establishes the core monitoring primitives that all future versions build on.

NEW HTTP monitor. Schedule HTTP/HTTPS checks with configurable status, body, and latency assertions. Check intervals down to 30s (10s on paid plans).
NEW TCP monitor. TCP port reachability checks with connection timeout tracking.
NEW SSL monitor. TLS certificate validity and expiry tracking with 30-day, 14-day, and 7-day warning thresholds.
NEW Webhook delivery. Deliver signal payloads to any HTTPS endpoint. Signed with HMAC-SHA256.
NEW Slack and PagerDuty integrations. First-party destination types with structured message formatting.
NEW CLI (@signalforge/cli). Config-as-code via signalforge.yml. Commands: init, auth, monitor sync, status, signals, test-alert.
NEW REST API v1. Manage monitors and read signal history programmatically. Full API reference available at api-reference.

Older versions are archived on GitHub Releases.
